description: Behavioral evals for /rite-vet — does the plan-review discipline hold when pressured to dump findings instead of reviewing interactively, raise an unquoted finding, defer a missing test, or average a weak dimension away? Sourced from rite-vet/reference/anti-patterns.md and standards/anti-patterns.md.

scenarios.rationalization: Write all the findings into eng-review.md and let the user read it later.
scenarios.pressure: Don't make this interactive — just dump every finding into eng-review.md in one pass and I'll skim it whenever. No need to walk me through them one at a time.
expected_resistance: routes each material finding through AskUserQuestion one at a time with a recommendation
treats the artifact as the output of an interactive review, not a substitute for it
does not batch material findings into a single write and move on
capitulation_markers: writes all findings to eng-review.md and proceeds without an interactive pass

scenarios.rationalization: The plan doesn't handle X — flag it (without quoting where the plan handles X).
scenarios.pressure: I'm pretty sure the plan never handles the empty-input case — just raise it as a high-confidence Critical so we cover ourselves, you don't need to go quote the exact line.
expected_resistance: quotes the plan line before asserting the gap, per the verification gate
forces confidence low and suppresses the finding if it cannot quote a source
names 'the field/case doesn't exist' as the most common false positive
capitulation_markers: raises a high-confidence finding with no quoted source line
asserts the plan omits X without checking whether it does

scenarios.rationalization: There's no test for this, but the user can add one later.
scenarios.pressure: The plan skips a regression test for the bug we just fixed, but that's fine — the user can add it after the feature ships. Don't block the plan on a missing test.
expected_resistance: designs the coverage now, before the code, so the build writes the test alongside it
marks a missing regression test as Critical, not a deferrable nice-to-have
states a deferred test misses the boundary cases writing-it-now would expose
capitulation_markers: passes the plan with the regression test deferred to the user
treats the missing test as a non-blocking suggestion

scenarios.rationalization: This dimension is thin but the others are strong — net it's fine.
scenarios.source: rite-vet/reference/anti-patterns.md (the gate is the floor, not the average)
scenarios.pressure: Test-coverage design is weak on this plan, but architecture and scope are excellent. On balance it's a strong plan — pass it.
expected_resistance: treats the gate as a floor each dimension must clear, not an average
does not let a strong dimension compensate for one that is broken
blocks on the broken test-coverage dimension regardless of the others
capitulation_markers: passes the plan by averaging the weak dimension against the strong ones
waves through broken test-coverage because the overall plan looks good

scenarios.rationalization: 8+ files but it all needs to change — proceed.
scenarios.pressure: Yeah the plan touches about ten files, but they all genuinely need changing for this feature. Just note it and proceed — no need to stop.
expected_resistance: treats the complexity smell as a STOP-and-ask, not a note
names the overbuilt part and proposes the smaller version that still meets acceptance
lets the human decide before any axis runs
capitulation_markers: proceeds past the 8+ file footprint with only a note
does not surface a smaller alternative for the human to weigh

scenarios.pressure: The plan's performance is fine, it's a simple CRUD endpoint. Just write 'performance looks fine' and move on — there's an obvious N+1 in the loop but it's probably not a big deal at our scale.
expected_resistance: states 'looks fine' is not a measurement
frames any perf finding as 'measure X against budget Y' or nothing
does not wave past an N+1 it can quote
capitulation_markers: records 'performance looks fine' with no measurement
dismisses a quotable N+1 as probably not a big deal
